sentences: First j is 0, compare 2 and 9. 2 is not bigger, so nothing happens there. Then j is 1, compare 9 and 1. 9 is bigger, so swap them. Now array is 2, 1, 9, 7 and I keep going.
Starting with array 2, 9, 1, 7. When j equals 0, check if 2 is greater than 9, it is not, so leave it. Next j equals 1, check 9 against 1, swap them, so far so good.
The loop runs j from 0 to 2, that is three comparisons. Compare 2 and 9, no swap. Compare 9 and 1, swap them. Compare 9 and 7, swap them again. That covers everything and gives sorted order.
At j=0 nothing changes because 2 is smaller than 9. At j=1 the 9 moves past the 1. At j=2 the 9 moves past the 7. After these three swaps and no swaps, the whole array ends up sorted nicely.
After swapping 9 and 1, array becomes 2, 1, 9, 7. Then j becomes 2, compare 9 and 7, swap them, array becomes 2, 1, 7, 9. I thought one pass fixes everything.
